title: PR-level latency sleuth: ensemble anomaly detector for continuous perf gating
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a lightweight, ensemble-based performance anomaly detector ("latency sleuth") to run as part of PR CI and post-merge baseline jobs. Aim: reduce false positives on transient noise while catching meaningful regressions in tokens/sec and p95 latency before merging.

Motivation and background:
- Current CI gating uses single-metric thresholds and occasional baselines which are noisy for microburst-prone workloads. This produces both missed regressions and noisy PR rejections.
- We need a deterministic, computationally cheap detector that combines multiple signals (tokens/sec, p95, p99, tail error rate, GPU memory high-water marks) and produces an explainable score per PR.

Design overview:
1) Ensemble scoring: compute three independent estimators and combine by weighted voting:
   - nonparametric baseline delta (median of historical baseline window vs. current sample) using trimmed means and MAD (median absolute deviation) for robust scale;
   - bootstrapped p95 confidence interval overlap test (bootstrapped samples of latency traces);
   - microburst signature detector: short-window high-percentile across synthetic microburst runs (10s microbursts seeded into requests) to capture tail sensitivity.
2) Adaptive sampling: start with a minimal sample budget in PR CI (N=30 short traces) and automatically escalate (N up to 200) if inconsistent signals are observed or if the ensemble score is borderline. This keeps CI cost low while preserving detection power for suspicious changes.
3) Baseline generation: per-branch rolling baseline keyed by (model, input-profile, runtime-config, hw-type). Use time-decayed weighting to prefer recent stable baselines and snapshot baselines on major merges.
4) Explainability and signal export: produce a compact HTML/Markdown report per run with the ensemble score, per-estimator values, confidence intervals, visual sparkline of latency distributions, and links to Grafana dashboards and the raw trace artifact.
5) CI integration: implement as a GitHub Actions step and a reusable CircleCI orb (depending on repo policy) that uploads run artifacts to s3/artifacts and annotates PRs with the result. Implement a configurable policy: fail-on-high-confidence-regression, warn-on-borderline, or never-block (for experimental branches).

Metrics and acceptance criteria:
- Detection sensitivity: For injected synthetic regressions of +15% p95 or -20% tokens/sec, detector should flag >=95% within escalated budget and >=70% at minimal budget.
- False positive rate: historical baseline backtest should yield FPR <= 3% for normal, non-regression commits.
- CI overhead: minimal-budget run should add <= 2 minutes to PR CI wall clock on average; escalated runs should be offloaded to parallel runners and not block the main merge job longer than 8 minutes extra.
- Report quality: every flagged run must produce a human-readable report and a single-line PR annotation linking to the artifacts.

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Week 1: Prototype ensemble estimators and the bootstrapped p95 module; run locally on existing benchmark traces. Deliverable: prototype library + unit tests.
- Week 2: Implement adaptive sampling controller and microburst injector harness; add synthetic regression injection tests. Deliverable: harness and test suite.
- Week 3: Integrate with CI (GitHub Actions) and artifact storage; generate PR report template. Deliverable: action + report generator + example annotated PR.
- Week 4: Backtest on 6 months of historical CI/benchmark traces, tune weights and thresholds, produce dashboard for false-positive/sensitivity heatmap. Deliverable: tuning document and Grafana dashboard links.
- Week 5: Rollout to Canary teams (two repos) with policy set to warn; collect feedback and iterate.

Rollout and safety considerations:
- Default policy during initial rollout: warn-only on repo set. Escalate to fail-on-high-confidence after 2 weeks and verification.
- Allow per-repo and per-branch whitelists for noisy workloads.
- Provide an escape hatch to re-run longer-duration baselines after a failed PR check.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for bootstrapping logic and MAD-based detectors.
- Integration tests that simulate noisy network and microburst conditions using the existing workload simulator (linking to ENG-52981).
- Backtest against historical regression incidents to compute time-to-detect and compare to previous gating approach.

Documentation and observability:
- Confluence: write a design doc (link in comments) that describes math and tuning knobs.
- Grafana: new dashboard panels for ensemble score distribution, minimal vs escalated run durations, and false-positive trend.
- Console: expose per-route PR gating flags in the Redwood Console to let SRE/Platform teams opt-in.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How aggressive should escalation be before we block CI? Conservative escalation reduces FPR but may miss short regressions. Proposed: escalate to N=200 on borderline only; consider blocking only if ensemble score > 0.9.
- Weighting of estimators: do we favor tokens/sec changes or p95 changes for our weighted vote? Proposed default weights: p95 delta 0.45, tokens/sec 0.35, microburst 0.2. Tune during backtesting.
- Storage cost of historical baselines per (model, profile) — consider pruning policies and retention tiers.

Acceptance criteria (concrete):
- Prototype library merged to infra/perf-lib and unit tests pass.
- CI Action and report annotation available and used in at least two repos as warn-only.
- Backtest report showing <=3% FPR and >=95% detection sensitivity for injected +15% p95 regressions under escalated runs.

Next steps (short):
- Ravi to prototype bootstrapped p95 and MAD estimator (owner).
- Maya to draft confluence design doc and create Grafana dashboard skeleton.
- Schedule sync with SRE and Platform to discuss retention and per-repo policy by 2026-03-05.
